question: Who is the chairperson of National Green Tribunal of India as a December 2020?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Adarsh Kumar Goel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Adarsh Kumar Goel is the current chairperson of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) as of December 2020.
 
• He was appointed as the chairperson of NGT on July 6, 2018.
 
• Justice Adarsh Kumar Goel is a former judge of the Supreme Court of India.
 
• He has played a significant role in various landmark judgments concerning environmental issues in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Green Tribunal (NGT)**

 
 
• Established on October 18, 2010, under the National Green Tribunal Act 2010, NGT is a specialized body equipped with the necessary expertise to handle environmental disputes involving multi-disciplinary issues.
 
• The principal bench of NGT is located in New Delhi, with zonal benches in Pune (West), Bhopal (Central), Chennai (South), and Kolkata (East).
 
• The objective of NGT is to provide effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources.
 
• NGT aims to enforce legal rights relating to the environment and give relief and compensation for damages to persons and property.
 
 
 
• **Role of NGT in Environmental Protection**
 
 
• NGT plays a critical role in reducing the burden of litigation in higher courts on environmental matters.
 
• It ensures the effective implementation of environmental laws and policies.
 
• NGT has the power to hear all civil cases relating to environmental issues and questions linked to the implementation of laws listed in Schedule I of the NGT Act.
 
• It can provide relief, compensation, and restitution of property damaged, and measures for restitution of the environment.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Jurisprudence in India**
 
 
• India's environmental jurisprudence is enriched by various landmark judgments which have emphasized the importance of sustainable development and environmental conservation.
 
• The judiciary in India has been proactive in addressing environmental concerns and has established the right to a clean and healthy environment as a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Key judgments like the Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum case and the Ganga Pollution case have set significant precedents in environmental law.
